rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Electric Charge & Elementary Charge:** Electric charge is an intrinsic physical property of elementary matter that governs all electromagnetic interactions. Charges exist in two polarities designated by Benjamin Franklin as positive (carried by protons, $+e$) and negative (carried by electrons, $-e$). The elementary charge quantum is $e \approx 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}$.…  ·  **Quantization of Charge:** Electric charge is not continuous; it exists only in discrete integral multiples of the elementary electronic charge: $q = \pm n e$, where $n \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\}$. Quantization was first demonstrated macroscopically by Robert Millikan's oil-drop experiment (1909).…
